accent: Purple ACCENT and MUTE buttons sit left of the voice buttons (IM review). Each sound has three dynamic levels: Accent, Normal, Mute (Polynominal). The exact accent gain and programming method are not documented in sources found; inferred per-step, per-instrument.

built_in_effects.name: Sample tone pots
built_in_effects.notes: Two rear mini-pots set the low-pass tone of the user samples only (one pot per pair of samples). No effects on the preset voices; Polynominal: no built-in effects.

global_features: No pitch, envelope or pan control on any voice (Music Technology 'Beauty and the Beat')
10 voice faders for 16 voices, plus Sample Level fader; 10 individual outs + L/R (IM review); Polynominal says 12 separate outputs (conflict)
Sampling: 20 kHz bandwidth, 4 x 0.2 s, 2 x 0.4 s or 1 x 0.8 s; mic/line input; samples kept at power-off
Sequencer: 99 (IM) or 100 (VSE/Polynominal) patterns, 20 songs; tempo 40-250 BPM; quantise ('Auto-compensate') 1/2 to 1/96 incl. triplets; real-time and step entry
MIDI In/Out/Thru on any channel; fixed note numbers following the Yamaha drum-machine standard (numbers not given in sources found); MIDI clock only, no DIN sync
16-voice polyphony (Polynominal)
Swing/shuffle and flam: not documented

global_features: 8-voice analog poly; poly-8, poly-4 and mono modes (mono stacks all 24 oscillators)
2 DCOs + sub-oscillator per voice; saw, sine, pulse with PWM; noise generator
SSM2044 24 dB/oct resonant low-pass filter per voice; self-oscillates around settings 98-99; dedicated ADSR
LFO (saw/square/triangle) with delay; portamento, glissando, hold; split and dual modes; 48 memories; 61 keys; basic MIDI
Sequencer conflict: VSE says real-time sequencer of 1,500 notes with 8 memories; sequencer.de lists none
How drums are made (inferred): noise plus fast VCF/VCA envelopes for snares and hats; self-oscillating filter or DCO with short decay for kicks and toms; ring-mod 'Brass' for metallic and zap sounds

accent: Desktop MD16 has 16 velocity-sensitive pads and a velocity curve (1-8) per voice; velocity can affect tuning, length, attack and start. An 'Accent/Level' key exists (Shift + Accent/Level cycles the four pad levels). How a dedicated accent works is not described in the reviews found. The MD16R/RP use non-velocity buttons (velocity via MIDI).

built_in_effects.name: Pad echo / echo banks
built_in_effects.notes: MIDI-style repeats on pad levels 3-4 (MT) or programmable echo banks assignable to any pad (SOS): rate 1-120 MIDI clocks straight/triplet, 1-16 repeats, fade -8..+8, can link to pitch changes. No reverb.

global_features: 41 ROM samples, 16-bit 44 kHz, no ambience; ROM cartridge port for extra samples
16 pads x 4 levels plus auxiliary set = 128 pad assignments; level 4 allows up to 3 samples per pad crossfaded by velocity
Chromatic Pad spreads one sound across 16 pads in semitones
Humanise: random start, random pitch, human level; Auto Pan/Pitch/Reverse
Swing +/-8 (MD16R/RP add negative swing), timing randomisation, cyclic randomisation, quantise down to 1/192
254 patterns (1-682 beats) and 254 songs, song chain x20, tempo track
8-note polyphony; stereo out + 8 mono outs on 4 stereo jacks; each out monophonic
MIDI In/Out/Thru, tape sync, SysEx and tape dumps
Shown at Frankfurt 1990 (SOS); Music Technology review March 1991 at GBP 299.95
pack_contents: 48 mono 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs named only by number, CHTMD01-CHTMD48, plus readme.txt: 'Unfortunately I no longer own this machine or its manuals and don't have a list of the sound names.' 48 files vs 41 documented ROM sounds: 7 unexplained. Rough grouping inferred from length and brightness only (low confidence): 01-05 kicks; 06-12 snare-type; 13-16 hi-hats (13 0.12 s, 14 0.30 s, 15 0.60 s, 16 0.18 s, fitting Closed/Mid/Open/Pedal); 17-20 toms; 21-28 low-mid toms or tonal perc; 29-32 cymbals; 33-47 percussion; 48 low (possibly the bass guitar). Numbering cannot be matched to official names without the ROM order.

built_in_effects.notes: Room 1-3, Hall 1-2, Plate, Delay, Pan-Delay. Fed by each section's FX1 send; within the Percussion Set each of the 12 instruments has its own FX1 send.

built_in_effects.name: FX-2
built_in_effects.notes: Chorus 1-4, Feedback Chorus, Flanger, Short Delay, Feedback Delay. Fed by FX2 sends (per section and per percussion instrument).

built_in_effects.name: FX-3 2-band parametric EQ
built_in_effects.notes: On the stereo sum (all sections equally).

built_in_effects.name: Overblast

global_features: Sections: Kick (mono), Snare (mono), HiHat (duophonic open/closed), Percussion Set (12-voice), Bass/Lead (mono synth); 16 drum/percussion voices + mono bass (manual specs)
Raw instruments: 26 kicks, 25 snares, 7 hi-hats, 128 drumset samples (126 names printed), 28 bass waves
64 user sounds per drum section; 10 editable percussion sets of 12; per-instrument wave, tune, level, pan, FX sends
Groove (shuffle %) per pattern track
Drumgrid 16 steps per bar; resolutions 8th, 12th (triplet), 16th, 24th, 32nd
Tempo 50-250 BPM with tap tempo; MIDI clock master or slave
Default MIDI channels: Kick 1, Snare 2, HiHat 3, Percussion 4 (shift with system channel); note range 36-96
100 ROM patterns, 99 preset motifs, 100 user motifs, 16 songs
Options: 2 individual outs, 2 audio inputs, 2 expansion slots (synth and drum expansions)
Polyphony conflict: manual says mono bass + 16 drum voices; VSE says 17 voices; Wikipedia says 32

Numbering does not line up with the manual's categories (28/26/25/7/128). B's count equals 128 + 7 numerically, but B001 is a low tonal sound while the first printed drumset entry is '606ClHH', so B is not in manual order. Header profile: A001-029 long (0.7-17.3 s), mostly noisy/bright; A030-050 short and very bright; B mostly 0.5-1.0 s with several clicks; B124-B135 are 12 files of about 30-150 ms at full scale with almost no zero crossings (click/pulse-like); C mixed, several low. Treat as unlabelled.

accent: No accent control; accent comes from MIDI velocity. Velocity (or a MIDI CC) can be assigned per parameter, e.g. snare tone and tune to velocity (SOS); the 'Velo...' and 'Tune Me Up' kits store such routings.

built_in_effects.name: Distortion
built_in_effects.notes: Soft-knee distortion on the currently selected drum voice (per voice); used in 'Power' (bass, snare, hats) and 'Hardcore' (bass drums) kits.

built_in_effects.name: Front Cut
built_in_effects.notes: Removes up to 99 ms from the start of a drum sound.

global_features: Analogue Sound Modelling (ASM) for bass drum, snare, toms, congas, hi-hats and cymbals, often layered with a sample; PCM only for cowbell, maracas, claves, ride, rim shot, hand clap (SOS)
Polyphony 'up to 8' (reviewer told) vs 12 in the manual; ASM drums reduce it
Per-drum setting to accept or ignore note-off (decides whether a retrigger cuts the sound)
25 preset + 15 user kits; SysEx dumps
Stereo out + 6 individual outs, assignable per drum and stored per kit; per-drum pan
About 100 MIDI CCs; all 22 knobs send CC; CC7 master volume
Assign Bank maps one drum across an octave; GM remap with 808/909 mode
Sync24 (DIN) clock out driven by incoming MIDI clock
No sequencer
Year: 1996 (SOS July 1996 review); Sonic State says 1995

ordered_list: Program 18 (pack Kit17): A Bit Off TR909
Program 19 (pack Kit18): A Bit off TR808
Program 24 (not in pack): Classic TR909 Ind. - individual outputs 1 = bass, 2 = snare, 3 = hi-hats (manual snippet)
Program 25 (not in pack): name unknown - individual-output duplicate kit per pack Readme
sound_bank.list_source: Kit names from the pack's Readme.txt; program numbering checked against manual factory-list snippets (https://manualshive.com/en/manual/novation/drumstation/1711554?page=46, page itself blocked); voices from https://notebook.zoeblade.com/DrumStation_MIDI_map.html

pack_contents: 23 folders Kit00-Kit22, each with 27 mono WAVs (621 total) named DS<kit><808|909><Sound>.wav, plus Readme.txt listing the kit names. 808: Kick, Snare, TomLo, TomMid, TomHi, CongaLo, CongaMid, CongaHi, Rimshot, Clave, Clap, Maracas, Cowbell, Cymbal, Hat_C, Hat_O. 909: Kick, Snare, TomLo, TomMid, TomHi, Rimshot, Clap, Hat_C, Hat_O, Crash, Ride. Every kit holds both 808 and 909 sets. Pack kit NN = factory program NN+1. Readme: 'Kits 023 and 024 are duplicate kits using individual outputs so have not been included' (= programs 24-25). Name glitches: Kit09 'DS09909TomHI.wav', Kit21 'DS21808Claves.wav'.
